caveats.text: The compiled exllamav3_ext binary present today (sha256 7d5fec66bfc5168ce5da008125e21290931a970e48202d3e74b70a0eff6f8015) differs from the builds recorded during the K6 (5a968c10...) and K8 (e0201c10...) encodes. All three are builds of the same pinned source, exllamav3 @ c5d9c657966ffeeaa9353f0cc899f18629da4a13 (v0.0.43), clean working tree; .so hashes differ through build non-determinism, not source drift. Both codecs in this head-to-head were driven through the SAME extension binary, so the comparison is exactly fair. This experiment compares the Python codec layer; it did not re-encode the shipped K6/K8 artifacts.

The only observed difference of any kind is the diagnostic field proxy_loss: Brandon's fast R10 path hardcodes proxy_loss=0.0 and records covariance_proxy_loss_evaluated=False; our reconstruction computes a real value (e.g. 9.5e-04). This field is metadata only -- it is not part of the packed payload, the suh/svh vectors, or the decoded weights, all of which are identical.

For K6/K8 the sealed public API refuses to encode at all. The extension-domain comparison therefore drives Brandon's sealed bound methods and sealed numeric core directly, skipping only the two non-numeric admission checks. This is a statement about his numeric machinery, not a claim that his shipped pipeline emits K6/K8: as published, it does not.

12 of the 24 matrices (layers 3/14/25/36) use a shape-matched production Hessian from layer 45 as a stand-in covariance, because the streaming campaign retained per-expert Hessians only for layer 45. Both codecs received bit-identical input, so fairness is unaffected; only the 'this is exactly a production encode' claim is weaker for those 12. The 12 tier-A matrices are production-exact.

extension_domain_run.method: Brandon's sealed bound methods and sealed numeric core, re-executing his encode_group body verbatim at K6/K8, skipping ONLY the two non-numeric policy checks (r10_codec.encode_group bit gate and types.EncodedTensor.__post_init__ ALLOWED_BITS). No sealed file was modified; hashes re-verified after the run.

fidelity_impact.reasoning: Every comparison is byte-identical, so the decoded-weight error delta between the two codecs is exactly 0.0 (not 'small' -- zero) on all 120 encodes. The KLD impact of the codec substitution is therefore identically zero: the substitution changes no encoded bit, so it cannot change any logit, and no re-scoring is required. For scale, the quantization error the codecs are jointly making is ~2.3e-02 relative Frobenius at K6 and ~7.2e-03 at K8; the inter-codec difference is 0 against that.

covariance.tier_A_production_exact: real production Hessians from out-k6/hessians/layer-045 (the only layer whose per-expert Hessians the streaming campaign retained), 12 matrices
covariance.tier_B_layer_coverage: real weights + real suh/svh from layers 3/14/25/36, with a real production Hessian used as a shape-matched stand-in covariance; identical for both codecs, so the head-to-head remains exactly fair -- only 'production realism' of H differs

inputs.normalization_vectors: real per-expert suh/svh read from the K6 campaign's own layer preparations (out-k6/preparation/layer-NNN/preparation.safetensors) -- the exact GSS/normalization artifacts the campaign encoder consumed

provenance_chain.note: these four hashes reproduce, byte for byte, the python_closure_sha256 block recorded in the K6 campaign's own out-k6/preparation/layer-NNN/preparation.json -- i.e. the reconstruction compared here is the same code that encoded K6
